ggmira: Plot multilayer networks in MiRA from R

Source: R/ggmira-package.R
ggmira-package.Rd

ggmira draws multilayer networks in MiRA, the browser-based multilayer network visualizer, and describes how they should look with code, the way ggplot2 does: start from the network with mira(), add components with +, and print the plot to open it in the browser. Everything can still be changed in MiRA's interface.

Plot basics

  • mira(): start a plot from a multilayer network. Or start in MiRA: plot_mira() opens a network with MiRA's defaults, and MiRA's R button gives the mira() code for the view made there.

  • +: add a component to a plot.

  • print.mira_plot(): open the plot in the browser (typing its name does this too). MiRA's R button copies the view back as R code.

  • mira_save(): save the plot as a PNG, JPG or PDF file, without opening a window.

  • mira_spec(): what the plot sends to MiRA.

  • mira_options(): what each component can be set to, for a network.

Elements (nodes, links, layers)

  • mira_node(): node color, size, shape, labels and a highlighted node.

  • mira_intralayer(): the links within layers.

  • mira_interlayer(): the links between layers.

  • mira_layer(): layer colors, names and arrangement.

Scales

  • mira_scales: how values become colors (color_values, color_scale, color_palette, color_reverse, color_limits) and sizes.

Layout

  • mira_layout(): where the nodes go.

Camera

  • mira_camera(): rotate, tilt, zoom and pan the view.

Legends

  • mira_legends(): which legends are open, and where.

Data (what is drawn)

  • mira_filter(): draw only some nodes, links or layers (network, grid and map views; layers also in the layer view).

Views (MiRA's modes)

One view per plot; the other components still apply where MiRA uses them (mira_mode: the rules, and what applies in each view).

  • mira_mode_grid(): the layers side by side.

  • mira_mode_map(): the layers on a geographic map.

  • mira_mode_layer(): one bubble per layer.

  • mira_mode_meta(): the network aggregated over layers; layers dims the nodes and links of the other layers.

  • mira_mode_dashboard(): summary charts.

  • mira_mode_data(): the data tables.

Opening a network with MiRA's defaults

  • plot_mira(): open a network with no components, in any view (plot_multilayer() is the same, in the network view).

Feedback

  • mira_feedback(): send feedback as a filled-in GitHub issue (with a GitHub account). The documentation pages have a Feedback button too.

Networks

ggmira works with the multilayer objects of the emln package (emln::load_emln(), emln::create_multilayer_network()). MiRA reads their four tables; a column added to net$nodes, net$state_nodes, net$extended or net$layers can be mapped like any other.

The full list of functions: help(package = "ggmira"). Please report MiRA issues at https://github.com/Ecological-Complexity-Lab/MiRA/issues.
